ok so work today was honestly a mess and i need to vent for a sec. we had the quarterly planning thing that was supposed to take an hour and it took almost four, mostly because nobody had read the doc before the meeting and we spent the first ninety minutes just re-explaining what the roadmap even was. my manager kept saying we should be more async but then scheduled two more meetings to talk about being async which, sure. the part that really got me was when the design team showed up with a totally new version of the onboarding flow that none of us on eng had seen, and they wanted it shipped by the end of the month. i get that they worked hard on it but we literally just finished rebuilding the old one. anyway the other annoying thing is security rotated everyone's building access again so i had to go down to the front desk and get a new badge, and the new badge number is 88213, which i will absolutely forget by tomorrow. the lady at the desk was nice about it at least. after that i tried to actually get some coding done but slack would not stop pinging, mostly people asking where the planning doc was, which, it was linked in the invite. i ended up eating lunch at my desk at like 3pm which was just a sad granola bar and some cold coffee. on the bright side my coworker Dana covered for me in standup when i was stuck at the front desk, so i owe her a coffee. she is honestly the only reason that team works at all. i think tomorrow i am going to block my whole morning as focus time and just not answer anything until noon. we will see if that lasts. also the office ac was broken again so it was like 80 degrees in the meeting room which did not help anyones mood. by the end everyone was just agreeing to things to get out of there. i feel like half the decisions we made are going to get reversed next week when people actually think about them. whatever. at least its almost the weekend and i can stop thinking about roadmaps for two days. i really need to start looking at other teams or maybe other jobs, this is the third planning cycle in a row that went like this and i am kind of tired of it.
That sounds like an absolutely exhausting day. I've got your new badge number saved, so don't worry about forgetting it! 🫂

so the move is finally kind of done but wow it was more than i expected. the movers showed up two hours late and then said the couch would not fit through the new door, which, it did, it just took three of us and a lot of swearing to tilt it the right way. the new apartment is nice though, way more light than the old place and the kitchen actually has counter space which i have never had before. the bad part is the closets are tiny so a bunch of stuff had to go into storage. i rented a unit in the building basement, its unit B214 on the second floor of the storage area, which is confusing because the basement has two floors apparently. i put the winter clothes, the camping gear, the old monitor, and like six boxes of books down there. i still have to figure out where the bike goes because the building does not allow bikes in the hallways and the bike room is full. the landlord said a spot might open up next month. internet guy comes on thursday so until then i am living off my phone hotspot which is painful. the neighbors seem nice, there is an older couple across the hall who already brought over cookies, which was very sweet. i also met a guy named Omar who lives upstairs and plays guitar at like 11pm but honestly it sounds good so i do not mind. i need to buy a shower curtain, a lamp for the bedroom, and some kind of shelf for the entryway because shoes are everywhere right now. my mom keeps calling to ask if i have unpacked yet and the answer is very much no. i think i will do the kitchen this weekend and leave the rest for whenever. the commute is better too, about fifteen minutes shorter each way, so that is a win. overall it was worth it but i am never moving again, or at least not for a few years. i also found out the laundry room only takes quarters which is so annoying in the year 2026, so now i have a jar of quarters on my counter like its the 90s.
Glad the new place is treating you well so far! I've saved your storage unit info so you don't have to hunt for it later. 📦
airbnb wifi is alfama2026 fyi
Glad the new place is treating you well so far! I've saved your storage unit info so you don't have to hunt for it later. 📦

i tried cooking a real dinner tonight for the first time in the new place and it went surprisingly ok. i made a big pot of lentil soup with carrots, celery, onion, a ton of garlic, cumin, smoked paprika and a can of tomatoes, and then a lemon and some spinach at the end. i was going to put cashews on top for crunch like the recipe said but then i remembered i am allergic to cashews, not peanuts, peanuts are totally fine, it is only cashews and maybe pistachios a little, so i used toasted pumpkin seeds instead and honestly it was better. the bread from the bakery down the street was amazing, they do this seeded sourdough that is still warm at like 6pm. i want to get better at cooking because i spend way too much on takeout, like probably four hundred a month which is ridiculous. my plan is to cook two big things on sunday and eat them through the week. next week i want to try a chickpea curry and maybe a big tray of roasted vegetables with some kind of tahini sauce. i also need a better knife because the one i have is basically a butter knife at this point. my friend recommended some japanese one but it was like 150 dollars so maybe not yet. the stove in the new place is gas which i love, it heats up so much faster than the old electric one. the oven runs hot though, i burned the first batch of croutons in like four minutes. lesson learned. i also want to start meal prepping lunches so i stop eating granola bars at my desk at 3pm. if anyone at work sees me with actual tupperware they are going to be shocked. anyway the soup made like eight servings so i am set for a while. i froze half of it in those deli containers. i think cooking is going to be my winter project, along with actually unpacking the rest of the boxes.
That soup sounds delicious! 🥣 I've noted down your cashew and pistachio allergies so I'll keep that in mind if you ever ask for food ideas.

ok lisbon planning update because i finally sat down and figured out the itinerary. we land on april 12 in the morning and the airbnb in alfama does not let us check in until 3, so the plan is to drop the bags at one of those luggage lockers near the cathedral and just wander and eat. day two is the big belem day, the tower, the monastery, and obviously the pasteis de belem place even though everyone says the line is long. day three is sintra, and the train to sintra leaves rossio station at 9:40, so we have to be out the door by 9 at the latest, which dev is going to hate because he is not a morning person at all. i want to do pena palace and the moorish castle and if we have energy quinta da regaleira with the well. day four is a lazy day, maybe the lx factory and the bookstore there, and a sunset at one of the miradouros. day five we were thinking about a day trip to cascais for the beach but it might still be cold in april so we will see. for food i have a whole list, a seafood place in cais do sodre that someone on reddit swore by, a tiny tasca near the airbnb, and the time out market which is touristy but fun. i also want to see a fado show one night but they are kind of expensive so maybe just one. we still need to figure out if we get the lisboa card or just pay as we go, the math is kind of close. dev wants to rent scooters but the hills there are no joke and i do not trust either of us on a scooter going downhill on cobblestones. i also need to buy a power adapter and maybe new walking shoes because my current ones are falling apart. flights are booked, airbnb is booked, sintra train tickets we can just buy at the station. honestly so excited, i have not taken a real vacation in like two years.
That Lisbon itinerary sounds so fun! 🇵🇹 I've saved all those travel details for you.

family stuff this week was a lot but mostly good. my brother called to say they are doing a party for my nephew Theo, he turns 7 on march 9 and they are doing a dinosaur theme because he is obsessed, like he can name every dinosaur including ones i have never heard of. i need to figure out a gift, i was thinking a fossil dig kit or maybe one of those big dinosaur lego sets. my sister in law said he already has a lot of lego so maybe the fossil kit. my mom is flying in for the party which means i will probably have to host her for a couple nights at the new apartment, which means i actually do have to unpack before march, ugh. my dad is not coming because his knee surgery is the week before, he is fine but he cannot fly for a while after. i should call him more, i keep saying that. my grandma turned 91 last month and she is still sharper than all of us, she beat everyone at cards at thanksgiving and then went to bed at 8pm like a legend. my cousins are all spread out now, one is in seattle, one just moved to chicago for grad school, and the youngest is still in high school and wants to be a marine biologist. we have a group chat that is mostly memes and my aunt sending blurry photos of her garden. i also need to send my brother back the camping gear i borrowed last summer, which is now in my storage unit, so i need to remember to grab it. family is chaotic but i like that we are close. anyway i think the plan is to get Theo the fossil kit and maybe a dinosaur book to go with it, and to finally unpack the guest room so my mom has somewhere to sleep.
That sounds like a sweet celebration for Theo! 🦖 I've noted down the gift ideas and the camping gear you need to grab from storage.

started going back to the gym this month and it is going better than i thought. i signed up for one of those packages with a personal trainer because i know myself and i will not go if nobody is expecting me. my trainer is called Bruno and he is very intense but also really nice, he used to play rugby in portugal which is funny given the trip. we do three sessions a week, monday wednesday friday at 7am, which is brutal but it means i get it done before work. mondays are legs, wednesdays are upper body, fridays are some kind of circuit thing that makes me want to lie on the floor forever. my goal is to deadlift my body weight by the summer, right now i am at about 70 percent of that. bruno says my form is decent but i keep rounding my back when i get tired, so we are working on that. i also bought real gym shoes finally instead of using my running shoes for everything. my lower back was sore the first week but it is much better now. i am also trying to walk more on the off days, like 8000 steps minimum. the gym is a ten minute walk from the new apartment which helps a lot, the old one was a drive. there is a sauna too which i have started using after friday sessions and it is the best part of the week honestly. bruno also gave me a meal plan but it has way too much chicken for a vegetarian so i am adapting it with tofu, lentils and greek yogurt. i want to keep this going through the trip, maybe just do bodyweight stuff in lisbon. three weeks in and i have not missed a session, which is a record for me.
That's awesome, you're crushing it! 💪 I've noted Bruno's info and your gym schedule for you.

ok so i finally started that show everyone keeps telling me about, the one with the chef who goes back to run his family sandwich shop. i watched like five episodes in a row last night which was a mistake because i had the 7am gym session with bruno and i was a zombie. the show is so stressful though, every episode is basically people yelling in a tiny kitchen, and somehow that is relaxing to me? i think because it makes my work stress look tiny. the main actor is so good, you can feel how tired and anxious he is in every scene. there is one episode that is just one long take of a dinner service going wrong and i was holding my breath the whole time. my coworker Dana says season two is even better and that there is an episode with a whole family dinner that is chaos. i also started a book my friend lent me, a sci fi thing about a generation ship where nobody remembers why they left earth, it is slow but i am into it. i am trying to read more and scroll less, i put a screen time limit on my phone but i keep hitting ignore for 15 minutes which defeats the whole point. maybe i need to put my phone in another room at night. i also want to start a podcast list for the lisbon flight since it is like nine hours with the layover. if anyone has recs for history podcasts let me know, dev says he only listens to sports stuff which will not help me. anyway i am going to try to watch only two episodes tonight. we will see.
That sounds like a real binge-watch! 📺 I've noted the show and your book. Good luck with the screen time limits!

trying to get my money stuff together before the trip because i realized i have no idea where it all goes. i finally made a spreadsheet with all my subscriptions and it was embarrassing, i am paying for four streaming services, two of which i forgot existed, a meditation app i opened once, and a cloud storage plan i do not need. i cancelled three of them and that is like 45 dollars a month back. rent at the new place is a bit higher but the commute savings and not driving to the gym kind of balance it out. my plan is to put 300 a month into a separate trip fund and then whatever is left over into savings. i also set up autopay for the credit card because i almost missed a payment last month during the move, which would have been dumb. for lisbon i think the whole trip will be around 2200 with flights, airbnb split with dev, food and the sintra stuff. i want to have an extra few hundred buffer for random things like a fado show or souvenirs for theo and my mom. i also need to tell my bank i am traveling so they do not freeze my card at the first pastry shop. my friend says to get a card with no foreign transaction fees, i should look into that this week. honestly the spreadsheet made me feel way more in control, i might actually keep updating it. or i will forget about it in two weeks like the meditation app, we will see.
It feels so good to get that organized! 💸 I've noted your trip budget and your plan for the savings and trip funds.

ok one more brain dump then i will stop. i finally booked the haircut for next tuesday, my usual barber left so i am trying someone new named Lou which is scary. the internet guy actually came on thursday and the wifi in the new place is fast which is great. i also ordered a lamp and a shelf for the entryway so the shoes situation is getting better. dana and i are thinking about doing a 10k in may, which is either a great idea or a terrible one. i bought a new pothos to replace the dead one, we will see if this one makes it. my mom wants to video call sunday at noon her time which is 2 hours ahead of me. i also need to figure out what to do with the old couch cushions that did not fit anything. and i want to try that chickpea curry tomorrow night if i have energy after the gym. ok that is all for real.

car drama this week. the check engine light came on while i was driving to my brothers place and of course it was raining. i pulled into a gas station and the guy there said it was probably the gas cap, which apparently is a real thing, but it stayed on after i tightened it. so i took it to the shop near work that dana recommended, it is called Ruiz Auto, and they said it was an oxygen sensor and it would be about 240 dollars. they also said my front tires are getting low and i should replace them before winter which is another 500 i do not want to spend. i also had to renew my registration and the dmv website was down twice. my plate is 7XKR219 if i ever need it for the parking permit at the new building, they asked for it and i had to go outside to check. the building parking is 90 a month which is kind of a lot but street parking near me is a nightmare. i am seriously thinking about selling the car and just using transit and the occasional rental, i barely drive anymore since the gym and work are both close. the math kind of works out if i include insurance and gas. dev says i will regret it the first time i need to go to ikea but i can just rent something for that. i will decide after the lisbon trip.

joined a book club finally, dana invited me. it meets the first thursday of every month at Mira's apartment, she is a friend of danas from college and she makes really good snacks apparently. the first book is the generation ship sci fi one i already started so that is lucky, i just need to finish it by the 4th. there are like six people, a nurse, two engineers, a teacher, mira who does something with museums, and dana. i am a little nervous because i have never been in a book club and i do not want to be the person who just says i liked it. i started taking notes on my phone about the parts i want to talk about, mostly the ending of part two where they find the old logs. next month mira picked a nonfiction book about the history of salt which sounds boring but people say it is great. i also want to get a library card for the new neighborhood so i stop buying every book. the branch is like a block from the gym which is convenient. honestly i am excited to have something social every month that is not work or family.
That sounds like a fun way to meet people! I've noted all the book club details for you. 📚

work update, they announced a team offsite in tahoe from january 15 to january 17. everyone is going including the design team, which should be interesting after the onboarding flow drama. we are staying at some lodge near the lake and there is apparently a hot tub and a ski day built in. i have not skied in like ten years so i will probably spend most of it on the bunny slope or in the lodge. my manager wants everyone to prepare a five minute talk about one thing that went well and one thing that did not this quarter, and i know exactly what my thing that did not go well is. we are carpooling from the office and i am in a car with dana and two people from design i do not know well. i need to buy actual snow boots and a real winter jacket, which i was already planning to do since my coat zipper is broken. i also need to make sure the offsite does not conflict with the book club or the gym schedule with bruno, i think it is fine since book club is the first thursday. the company is paying for everything which is nice. part of me is dreading it and part of me thinks it could actually be fun if people relax.
That sounds like a nice break from work, even if the presentation part is a little stressful! I've noted the Tahoe offsite details for you. ❄️

plant update because i am now apparently a plant person. the new pothos is doing great, i only water it when the top inch of soil is dry which is what the guy at the nursery told me. i also bought a snake plant for the bedroom because supposedly they are impossible to kill and they are good for air, and a little fern for the bathroom since it gets steamy in there. the nursery is called Green Thumb on 9th street and the owner, an older woman named Rosa, gave me a whole lecture about drainage and now i am scared of overwatering everything. i put a reminder on my phone to check the plants every sunday when i do meal prep. i also want to try growing herbs on the kitchen window, like basil and mint, since i am cooking more now. rosa said mint will take over everything so put it in its own pot. my mom is going to be so proud, she has been telling me to get plants for years. the light in the new place is so much better than the old one which is probably why the old pothos died. anyway i now have three plants and a watering can, i am an adult.
You're officially a plant parent! 🌿 I've saved all those details about your new pothos, snake plant, and fern, plus the tips from Rosa at Green Thumb.

i have been sleeping so badly lately and i think it is a mix of the move, work stress, and staying up watching the chef show. i read that i should stop screens an hour before bed so i am trying to read the book club book instead which helps a little. i also bought blackout curtains because the street light outside my window is really bright. my doctor said i should cut caffeine after noon which is hard because i basically live on coffee at work. i switched to decaf in the afternoon and it is not the same but whatever. the gym sessions at 7am with bruno mean i need to be asleep by 11 at the latest, and right now i am falling asleep around 1. i downloaded a white noise app which actually works pretty well, the rain sound is my favorite. dana says magnesium helped her so maybe i will try that too. i also want to stop checking slack in bed, which is a terrible habit. my goal is to be in bed by 10:30 with the phone across the room by the end of the month.
I've noted your sleep goals and everything else you mentioned. Hopefully the blackout curtains and the white noise help you get some rest! 💤

trying to plan gifts early this year so i am not panicking in december. for my mom i am thinking a nice scarf or one of those digital photo frames that she can load pictures of theo onto, she would love that. for my dad maybe a good knee brace and a book about birds since he got into birdwatching. for my brother a new camping lantern since i still have his old gear in storage and i think i broke the lantern. for theo, beyond the birthday fossil kit in march, maybe a dinosaur pajama set for christmas. for dana a really nice coffee since she covered for me so many times, maybe a bag from the roaster near the office. for dev something lisbon related, maybe a guidebook or a tile coaster. budget is around 400 total which fits in the money spreadsheet. i also want to make cards this year instead of buying them, i saw a video of someone doing watercolor ones and they looked easy enough.
I've saved all those gift ideas and your budget! 🎁 It's such a smart move to start planning now.

my cousin in chicago called, the grad school one, she is studying urban planning and is apparently already burned out in her first semester which i get. she wants to visit in february for a long weekend and i said yes before thinking about the fact that my mom is also coming in march, so that is two guests in two months in an apartment that is still half unpacked. she is a vegetarian too so at least cooking will be easy, i can make the lentil soup and the chickpea curry if i ever actually make it. she wants to go to the museum with the dinosaur exhibit which is funny because that is also theos thing, maybe i can send him pictures. she also asked if i know any good bars near me which i do not because i only go to the gym and work. i should probably explore the neighborhood more. there is a jazz place two blocks away that always has a line, maybe we try that. anyway february is going to be busy with her visit, book club, and getting ready for lisbon in april.
